newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends at intraday low, selling gathers pace.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends at intraday low, selling gathers pace.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at an intraday low of 8.2914 to the dollar on Monday against 8.2905 on Friday, pressured by a late bout of speculative selling, dealers said.
The central bank's repeated intervention to halt the yuan's rise above the 8.2900 level hurt confidence and speculators stepped in to force the currency lower, they said.
"Sentiment was hurt as the yuan failed to breach the key psychological resistance level of 8.2900," one dealer said.
Yuan buyers would stop efforts to try to test that level in the short term, dealers said.
"Comments from an official of the central bank on maintaining the stability of the yuan also prevented upward momentum," another dealer said.

Chen Yuan, vice president of the central bank, was quoted by the Shanghai Securities News on Saturday as saying the exchange rate of the yuan was at an appropriate level and the central bank would maintain its stable movements despite pressure to appreciate.

The yuan opened unchanged at 8.2903 and rose slightly to hit an intraday high of 8.2902 in early trade. It fell to move at around 8.2905 for most of the session and slipped to close at a low for the day.
The weighted average price on Friday was 8.2903, they said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to rebound slightly on Tuesday.
The yuan closed little changed at 6.9900 from 6.9870 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly up at 1.0702 from 1.0704 against the Hong Kong dollar.
